html:
The Iași pogrom was a massacre of Jews in the city of Iași in northeastern Romania that began on 27 June 1941, days after Romania joined Germany in invading the Soviet Union.

Romanian police, soldiers and civilians, with some German troops, killed Jews in the streets and in the police headquarters courtyard. Thousands more were packed into sealed freight trains that rolled for days in the summer heat, and most died of thirst and suffocation. Romania later put the number of dead at over 13,000. The regime of Ion Antonescu went on to kill and deport Jews and Roma in Bessarabia, Bukovina and Transnistria, making Romania responsible for one of the largest death tolls of the Holocaust outside Germany. Romania officially accepted this only in 2004, after the Wiesel Commission report, ending decades of denial since World War II.
sum: The Iași pogrom was a massacre of Jews in the city of Iași in northeastern Romania that began on 27 June 1941, days after Romania joined Germany in invading the Soviet Union.
